about.title: Anaheim Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death in Anaheim is caused by someone else's carelessness, the people left behind are asked to make decisions at the worst possible time. Public records show 34 traffic deaths across the city in 2025, with collisions clustering along SR-91 in both directions, Ball Road and Lincoln Avenue, and reports tending to peak on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. Behind each of those numbers is a household in Orange County trying to figure out what comes next. A wrongful death claim is a civil action, separate from anything a prosecutor may or may not pursue. Under California law, a spouse or domestic partner and children hold the first right to bring it, followed by certain dependents and heirs, and the filing window is generally two years from the date of death—shorter when a government entity is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Anaheim families, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so no fee is owed unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Anaheim Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney you are connected with can confirm where your family fits before any step is taken.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is considerably shorter when a city, county, or state agency is involved. Getting connected promptly protects that timeline.

items.title: A full picture of recoverable losses
items.desc: Funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance can all be part of a claim. An independent attorney reviews each of these with you, not just the receipts.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on SR-91 near Anaheim and the driver is facing charges. Do we still need a civil case?
items.answer: Yes, the two proceed on separate tracks. A criminal case is brought by the district attorney and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action your family brings to recover losses such as funeral costs and lost support. The outcome of one does not decide the other, and an attorney can explain how the two may interact.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children of the person who died have the first right to file. If there are none, certain dependents and heirs may qualify instead. Because standing rules can get complicated in blended families, it is worth having an independent attorney review your specific situation.

items.question: How long do we have to act after a death in Anaheim?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. That period is much shorter if a government entity—such as the City of Anaheim, Orange County, or Caltrans—may share responsibility, because a formal claim must be presented first. Reaching out early gives an attorney room to investigate before any deadline becomes an issue.
